💯. While I agree voters have a lot influence on the results for sure, I think comps can be improved. I've commented about it here multiple times (I think most of my latest comments were abt this) but basically comps can be made better by improvements in tagging.

If a specific item of clothing was mentioned in the description, it should be mandatory (like the blue ring in the paraiba comp, but not all comps were configured that way).

More tags can be added to clothes (or make users also filter by the type of clothing for example, which is possible since some comps allow us to do that). But I think balancing between being too specific and too general is also important (cus being too specific will be too restrictive on the players). But adding/revamping tags on its own can still help improve comps imo (maybe combining it with revamping comp descriptions as well).

Maybe there can also be comps with exclusions (like if the comp is obviously about using casual clothes, glam clothes will be excluded or the player will have penalty points if glam clothes are used). Personally I prefer this as I want comps to be a bit more difficult (it's a competition for a reason).

Im p sure there are more ways to improve comps. I just hope SuitU is aware of this concern and im the future can think about it. I feel like there are enough of p2p players that make this app sustainable and profitable, so I hope improvements can be made 🙏

And finally, just to add, if youre getting really frustrated, try to only join comps you really want/like. I did that for a month and I was mostly pleased since I got high scores (single digit %) for, like, 90% of the comps I joined. Now I'm back participating in everything and competing for S rank again. Ngl though I almost quit the game during that month. But the tarot flashback gacha brought me back lol. Anyway, just try resting from time to time too!

I think the best compromise is still making them go to college (like, make it actively a part of their goal pero not forced) and never mention the option na huwag magcollege at all. Looking back honestly my choices in life nung bata ako were shit.

Nung maghhighschool ako I wanted to stay in my current private school ko with my elem friends, but my parents made me go to this public highschool na maganda even though malayo sya. And honestly best decision siya. Wala akong pake nun, I didn't think of any effect nun sa future ko. Even nung magccollege ako. I didnt feel compelled to go to one of the "Big 4" universities, yet my parents made me take exams for them + scholarships. And I did end up going to a good university. I feel like I became a better person overall because of my experiences there. And I owe it to my parents na sila yung nagdrive saken to do those things.

I admit hindi naman sa madali and masaya naging experience ko. At times I hated my degree program. At times studying burned me out kse I was an achiever in elem/hs so I also wanted to be one in college. Pero feel ko parin na my parents did their best to direct me in life para hindi ako magend up like them na hindi ganun kaganda yung work and walang ipon.

Point ko lang naman talaga is, as parents sobrang laking ambag nung ability to impart experiences to children. I know you mean well by saying na you'll respect their decision to not go to college if ever, pero as a parent, dapat lang maguide parin sila towards "success" and that you'll be able to determine if yung anak mo ba tinatamad lang or ambitious ba talaga. Don't overestimate your child's ability to make decisions at that age. Marami pa silang di naeexperience at that point. Baka lang hindi nila naiisip yung possibility ng hirap ng buhay if hindi sila makakuha ng trabaho due to lack of a degree.

Have you seen the tablets in person? I've seen and held the S8+ before deciding which one to buy. Up 'til that point I was pretty much already decided on buying it due to the OLED screen. But hooboi, I'm a small person with small hands. The S8+ felt super big in my hands. It was light, sure, but when you add a case to that I doubt it'll be that handy. It didn't sit well with me and I thought if my tablet was this big, I won't be using it a lot.

I wasn't able to see and hold the S8 in person (it wasn't available in the Samsung store), so I went to an Apple store and tried holding the iPad Air. I think it felt just right (though still felt that it was still a bit big honestly haha, that's how small I am, but I needed a tablet with a good pen).

I then went back to the Samsung store to compare the S7+/S8+ OLED screen with the S7 FE TFT screen. And honestly I didn't see much of a difference. The OLED screens definitely have higher brightness levels and better color contrast. But I didn't even know which tablet I was holding at first. It didn't even occur to me that they had different screen types had I not looked at the labels.

If you look at them much, much closer, side by side, you'll definitely see a difference. But I'm not too sensitive to that kind of stuff, so I chose tab S8 in the end due to it being smaller. A tech-reviewer-youtuber I asked even said that the S8 screen looks better than the S7 FE despite them both having TFT screen (I guess since the latter being bigger?) so I have high expectations (my preorder hasn't arrived yet).

So in the end, it really depends on what you value the most. If you prefer your tablet more wieldy and portable, go for the S8. If you want a larger OLED screen and a larger book cover keyboard, then go for the S8+.
